an1.333:1.1: The “Black Plum Tree Land” is _jambudīpa_, the South Asian subcontinent, including India, Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh, and Afghanistan.
an1.335:1.1: The “central countries” (_majjhimā janapadā_) are defined in [pli-tv-kd5:13.12.1]()–6 as bounded to the east by Kajaṅgalā and Mahāsālā ([mn152:1.2]()), to the south-east the river Sallavatī (“abounding in frogs”, also spelled Salaḷavatī, “abounding in frankincense”), to the south the town Setakaṇṇika (“white-ear”), to the west the brahmin village of Thūṇa (“sacrificial post”; not the same place as in [ud7.9:1.2](), which is in the central Mallian region), and to the north the mountain Usīraddhaja (“vetiver crest”, possibly the Hindu Kush, named for appearing like the tall clumps of flower-tipped vetiver). This is less helpful than it might be, as most of these places are unknown. The same passage, however, makes it clear that Avantī is *not* one of the central countries; the same is the case for Gandhāra and Kamboja (Persia). They are laid out clockwise starting from the east, as is the method with the better-established places at [dn19:36.3](). See also the “civilized region” of [dn16:1.28.7](), the “Black Plum Tree Land” of [an1.333:1.1](), and the “sixteen great countries” of [an3.70:28.2]().
an1.335:1.2: “Foreigner” is _milakkha_ (Sanskrit _mleccha_), which is a primarily linguistic term for those who do not speak _ariyaka_, namely the Indo-Aryan languages such as Pali or Sanskrit ([pli-tv-bu-vb-pj1:8.4.10]()).
an1.342:1.2: For the distribution of negatives, see Bodhi’s note in his *Numerical Discourses*.
an1.345:1.1: The absorptions are stages of letting go; see [sn48.9:4.2]().
